audits.title: The Cataract National Dataset electronic multi-centre audit of 55,567 operations: updating benchmark standards of care in the United Kingdom and internationally.
audits.standard: Benchmark standards from the 1997-1998 UK National Cataract Survey
audits.setting: 12 NHS Trusts using electronic patient record systems (Cataract National Dataset)

cycle1.result: Posterior capsule rupture and/or vitreous loss 1.92%; zonule dialysis 0.46%; retained lens fragments 0.18%; postoperative VA 6/12 or better in 91.0% (6/6 or better 45.9%).

audits.other_findings: Phacoemulsification in 99.7%, local anaesthesia in 95.5%, trainees performed 33.9%; PCR/vitreous loss halved compared with the 1997-1998 survey.
audits.citation: Jaycock P, Johnston RL, Taylor H, Adams M, Tole DM, Galloway P, et al.. The Cataract National Dataset electronic multi-centre audit of 55,567 operations: updating benchmark standards of care in the United Kingdom and internationally. Eye (Lond). 2009;23(1):38-49. doi:10.1038/sj.eye.6703015. PMID: 18034196.

audits.title: Cataract surgery at Marie Adelaide Leprosy Centre Karachi: an audit.
audits.standard: CBM guidelines based on WHO monitoring for quality monitoring

cycle1.result: Good visual acuity at discharge in 962 (66%); best corrected acuity good in 97.2%. Posterior capsular rent with vitreous loss 70 (4.8%).

audits.other_findings: 565 (38.7%) lost to follow-up after discharge; striate keratopathy 157 (10.7%).
audits.citation: Paracha Q. Cataract surgery at Marie Adelaide Leprosy Centre Karachi: an audit. J Pak Med Assoc. 2011;61(7):688-690. PMID: 22204247.

audits.title: A 5-year audit of cataract surgery outcomes after posterior capsule rupture and risk factors affecting visual acuity.

cycle1.result: 887 capsule ruptures (rate 1.8%); visual success 93.9% after rupture versus 98.5% in uneventful cases.

audits.other_findings: Residents had higher rupture rates but similar visual success; risk factors for poor vision were age over 65, dropped nuclei and other complications.
audits.citation: Ti SE, Yang YN, Lang SS, Chee SP. A 5-year audit of cataract surgery outcomes after posterior capsule rupture and risk factors affecting visual acuity. Am J Ophthalmol. 2014;157(1):180-185.e1. doi:10.1016/j.ajo.2013.08.022. PMID: 24182746.

audits.title: Complication rate of posterior capsule rupture with vitreous loss during phacoemulsification at a Hawaiian cataract surgical center: a clinical audit.
audits.standard: Published PCR with vitreous loss rates
audits.setting: The Surgical Suites, ambulatory surgical centre, Honolulu (four private practice surgeons)

cycle1.result: 23 of 3,339 cases had PCR with vitreous loss, incidence 0.68%.

audits.other_findings: Main causes were miosis, shallow chamber, restlessness, pseudoexfoliation, floppy iris and zonulopathy; surgeon volume inversely correlated with PCR.
audits.citation: Chen M, Lamattina KC, Patrianakos T, Dwarakanathan S. Complication rate of posterior capsule rupture with vitreous loss during phacoemulsification at a Hawaiian cataract surgical center: a clinical audit. Clin Ophthalmol. 2014;8:375-378. doi:10.2147/opth.s57736. PMID: 24523578.

audits.title: Indicator-based audit of cataract surgery in four neighbouring hospitals in East Anglia.
audits.standard: VA 6/60 or worse wait under 3 months; VA 6/18 or worse wait under 12 months; 6/12 or better corrected VA at 3 months; under 2% sight-threatening complications; no life-threatening complications
audits.setting: Four neighbouring ophthalmic units in East Anglia

cycle1.result: 69.5% met 3-month wait standard; 85.8% met 12-month standard; 88.6% achieved 6/12 or better; 4.2% sight-threatening complications (target under 2%); 100% free of life-threatening complications.

audits.other_findings: Analysis led to some changes in cataract management in the four units, but no re-audit is reported.
audits.citation: Sarkies N, Everson J, Davies S. Indicator-based audit of cataract surgery in four neighbouring hospitals in East Anglia. Eye (Lond). 1995;9 ( Pt 6 Su):13-21. PMID: 8729013.
